These phenomena are realized when the subgap charge transport is predominantly contributed by the crossed Andreev scattering. In contrast, on the doublet side, we obtain signatures for the Kondo effect manifested by the low-temperature enhancement of the charge conductance and clearly evident in the thermopower. Such temperature-dependent local and nonlocal transport properties can unambiguously identify the specific configuration of the correlated quantum dot and reveal the rich physics emerging in the doublet-to-singlet crossover region.

title: Dynamical mean-field theory for associative memory with block-correlated patterns
abstract: In associative memories storing correlated patterns, retrieval of individual memories can compete with symmetric mixed states. A dynamical description is needed to determine how the initial state selects between these outcomes. We extend the generating-functional dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for independent patterns to independent blocks of correlated binary patterns of fixed finite size. The resulting effective single-neuron process has a self-consistent cross-talk noise covariance and self-feedback coefficients that depend on the block-covariance eigenvalues. For hierarchically correlated patterns with nonmonotonic transfer, increasing the loading can permit retrieval from an imperfect initial state before further loading prevents it. DMFT reproduces the retrieval trajectories and basin geometry found in direct simulations. Near the lower boundary of this re-entrant region, direct networks reveal stationary saddles separating coexisting mixed and target-retrieval states. Parameter sensitivities of DMFT trajectories predict nearby shifts of this boundary. At the tested upper boundary, retrieval remains accessible from initial states with larger target overlap, indicating a change in basin access. Under fixed-point convergence assumptions, the theory recovers the equations of generalized self-consistent signal-to-noise analysis.

title: Localizing Concepts in Visual Autoregressive Models
abstract: Understanding the internal routing of visual concepts is crucial for the safe and controllable adaptation of generative models. While concept localization has been widely studied in diffusion models, the emerging paradigm of next-scale visual autoregressive models remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce LoCo, the first model-agnostic framework to localize where and when specific concepts emerge within autoregressive models. Driven by the native coarse-to-fine nature of next-scale generation, our method precisely maps conceptual knowledge across three distinct dimensions: Layer, Scale, and Position. To systematically localize and evaluate concept routing without context bias, we propose LoCoBench, a comprehensive dataset spanning 10 diverse categories. Extensive probing on image and video autoregressive models like Infinity, HunyuanImage-3.0, and InfinityStar shows that the localized positions are both interpretable and causally related to concept emergence. Building on these insights, we apply our localization method to three key applications: concept erasure, model personalization, and adversarial concept injection. Experiments demonstrate that our targeted intervention achieves state-of-the-art performance, substantially reducing computational overhead while preserving benign utility. Overall, our findings offer insights into how conceptual knowledge is routed during autoregressive generation, introducing a practical pathway for more interpretable, efficient, and secure adaptation.

title: Higher-order jet and its application to the Novikov conjecture
abstract: In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the deffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher order $μ$-discreteness for subgroup $Γ< {\rm Diff}(M)$. As applications, we show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher order $μ$-discreteness.

title: Extracting non-Gaussian information of line-intensity maps with weighted skew spectra
abstract: The bispectrum of line-intensity maps carries cosmological and astrophysical information beyond the power spectrum, but its large data vector hampers the analysis of survey data. Skew spectra address this by compressing the bispectrum into a handful of power-spectrum-like observables, cross-spectra of the observed field with filtered squares of it. We present the first application of optimally weighted skew spectra to line-intensity mapping of galaxy-hosted emission, where all clustering and shot-noise terms are luminosity weighted and the mean intensity is unknown. We perform idealized real-space Fisher forecasts for a SPHEREx-like survey of H$α$ emission at $0.2 \lesssim z \lesssim 4.6$, in its deep fields and in a noisier all-sky configuration. First, the compression carries over to intensity maps: on perturbative scales and for a fixed redshift evolution of the emitters, four skew spectra, one of them matched to the shot noise, recover the bispectrum constraints on biases, shot noise and cosmological parameters to within a few percent. Second, the joint analysis of the power spectrum and the skew spectra measures the ratios of the second-order biases to the linear bias in each redshift bin. Within a bin the biases are degenerate with the unknown mean intensity, but their ratios are not, so their redshift evolution is measured without a model for the emitters. For emission that depends on halo mass alone, these ratios are determined by luminosity-weighted averages of the halo biases, so their evolution can test the halo-emission connection, including dependence on assembly history or environment. The bias ratios are not accessible to the tree-level real-space power spectrum alone. At $z \lesssim 3$ an all-sky SPHEREx-like configuration can detect departures of order $0.1$ in the bias ratios at $3σ$, while deeper fields perform better in the highest-redshift bins.

title: At the EDGES of MADness: phenomenology of relic millicharged atomic dark matter
abstract: Millicharged dark matter lives in a corner of parameter space that has been considerably shrinking over the past decades, due to constraints from cosmology, astrophysical systems, and ground-based experiments. A particularly interesting probe is the 21-cm absorption signal at Cosmic Dawn, which attracted interest in light of the EDGES claim: the reported excess absorption can be explained by millicharged dark matter with a fractional electric charge of~$10^{-6} \lesssim ε\lesssim 10^{-4}$, but it must be a subpercent of the total dark matter abundance to remain consistent with the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We show that very low fractions of millicharged dark matter naturally arise from atomic dark matter: a dark sector model that replicates the physics of standard atomic hydrogen. Dark ions undergo the process of dark recombination, leaving a relic ionized component that, in the presence of kinetic mixing, is naturally millicharged. We modify the cosmological Boltzmann solver CLASS to incorporate this scenario, and we investigate the parameter space of millicharged atomic dark matter (MAD) that is allowed by CMB, large-scale structure, and supernovae data. We find there are cosmologically viable regions of MAD parameter space that are consistent with laboratory and astrophysical bounds and also overlap with the EDGES-defined window. Although the EDGES result is likely not a Cosmic Dawn signal, MAD leaves distinctive cosmological signatures, accessible to upcoming 21-cm observations.

title: The $K T_{cc}(3875)$ Interaction: Bound State, Scattering Observables and Correlation Function
abstract: We investigate the interaction of a kaon with the $T_{cc}(3875)$ state, evaluating the scattering amplitude and the correlation function of the system within a molecular picture in which the $T_{cc}(3875)$ is regarded as a $D^* D$ bound state. Since the $KD^*$ and $KD$ interactions dynamically generate the $D_{s1}(2460)$ and $D_{s0}^*(2317)$ resonances, respectively, both of which are significantly bound with respect to their corresponding particle thresholds, the $KT_{cc}(3875)$ interaction is found to be strongly attractive, leading to the formation of two bound states with binding energies of about 63 MeV and 51 MeV, respectively, with respect to the $KT_{cc}(3875)$ threshold. We also determine the scattering observables at threshold, including the scattering length and effective range, and calculate the correlation function. The latter exhibits features similar to those found in previous studies of the scattering of an external particle off a dynamically generated resonance of molecular nature.

title: Quantum Metric Scaling and Its Exceptions in Classical Flat Bands
abstract: The quantum metric length has been proposed as the localization length scale in one-dimensional flat bands. Here, we study this quantum metric scaling and the exceptions to it in a classical flat band formed by a locally resonant mass--spring system. We find that the localization length follows the quantum metric length near the flat band but departs from this proportionality at the exact flat-band frequency. Selective mass disorder also produces divergent localization lengths or arbitrarily short tails near the flat-band frequency without changing the clean metric. These exceptions show that disorder can select localization scales beyond those predicted by the quantum metric alone.

title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
abstract: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

title: BRACHIO: Broad Representations Across Centres for Head-and-neck Imaging Oncology (HECKTOR 2026)
abstract: The HECKTOR 2026 challenge benchmarks machine learning for head and neck cancer, where teams delineate primary and nodal tumour volumes, perform TN staging, and predict recurrence-free survival (RFS). This report describes the submissions for the HECKTOR challenge of team nucli. As the three tasks span both dense and global information from multicentric PET/CT scans, we utilise self-supervised pre-trained encoders, training a 2D DINOv2 encoder (PET-DINOv2-MIPs) on HECKTOR 2026's PET scans. Our final test submission ensembles a DynUNet trained from scratch with a SwinUNETR whose Swin trunk was initialised from a SimMIM-pre-trained checkpoint for segmentation, reaching a mean Dice of 0.5409. For TN staging, GTVp/GTVn geometric features from the segmentation masks are fit to stage probabilities by logistic regression (LR) and fused with PET-DINOv2-MIPs deep features (PCA + LR) via a second-level LR, reaching balanced accuracies of 0.3962 (T-stage) and 0.6432 (N-stage). For the RFS prognosis task, we fine-tune the last two blocks of the PET-DINOv2-MIPs ViT-S encoder jointly with an MLP head under a CoxPH loss, concatenating clinical covariates with the imaging features, reaching a test Harrell's C-index of 0.6577 and a weighted challenge score of 0.5802. The prognosis result is comparable to the best entry of the previous edition and consistent with our internal cross-validation, while our segmentation result is well below it and limits the staging results that depend on it.

title: Photon Rings and Mass-Independent Observables of a Five-Dimensional Charged AdS Black Hole
abstract: We investigate the optical properties of a five-dimensional charged anti-de Sitter (AdS) black hole. Using the null geodesic equations, we determine the event horizon and photon sphere radii and the critical impact parameter, showing that all decrease with increasing charge, while the photon sphere radius remains independent of the AdS radius. To avoid dependence on the mass scale and the observer-dependent apparent size of the shadow in an AdS spacetime, we introduce two mass-independent geometric observables: the subring exponent $γ$ and the ratio of the critical impact parameter to that of the direct image of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We derive $γ$ in closed form and show that it is independent of the AdS radius and satisfies $2π/\sqrt{3}<γ\leqπ\sqrt{2}$, above the values for four-dimensional Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström black holes. Using a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) forecast based on noiseless mock data with illustrative fractional uncertainties of $5\%$, we find that the dimensionless AdS radius can be constrained with a relative uncertainty of $16$--$19\%$, whereas the charge can be distinguished from zero only for the near-extremal fiducial model considered. Under these assumptions, the subring exponent provides a Gaussian separation of $3.4$--$5.9σ$ from the four-dimensional Schwarzschild black hole.

title: Graphical Modeling from Marginal Information via Optimal Transport
abstract: A graphical model represents multivariate interactions through conditional independence, but requires jointly observed samples to be fitted to data. When individuals cannot be tracked and only marginal observations are available, as with destructive measurements leading to cross-sectional data, the problem of graphical modeling is confounded with that of assembling a joint law. We show how simultaneous graphical modeling and joint law assembly can be realized via a multi-marginal optimal transport problem with graphical cost. Focusing on Gaussian marginals, we generate a joint law satisfying the Markov properties prescribed by a given graph. Within the class of joint distributions respecting the graph and marginals constraints, our construction selects a member by making the interactions set by the graph as strong as possible under a dependence budget measured by relative entropy. In the empirical setting, where only estimates of the marginals are available, we examine the stability of the problem under perturbations of both the marginals and of the graph weights. The resulting error splits into an estimation term, vanishing with the sample size, and a specification term, which quantifies the cost of a misspecified graph. Finally, we illustrate these findings by numerical experiments.

title: Agentic process evidence
abstract: The way software gets built is changing dramatically. AI agents now create pull requests, select dependencies, refactor codebases, interpret test failures, and execute infrastructure changes across the entire Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). AI agents are autonomous team members, but unlike human engineers, they are ephemeral - their reasoning, decisions, and tool calls vanish the moment the session ends. Modern Security incidents involving intent mismatch or injection are becoming increasingly common - forcing us to address AI Agents as an insider threat. No widely adopted standard yet enables agentic provenance and governance and its obvious that you can't hold an ephemeral process accountable. The git log was designed for human commits. It shows what changed. It does not show what an AI agent did, which model it used, which tools it called, or whether anyone was accountable for the outcome. Every governance framework, every audit trail, every compliance control in the SDLC was built around one assumption: a human made the decision. That assumption no longer holds. This shift introduces 3 main procedural problems (not addressing scale) - Supply-chain vector - The agentic coder is software, so it is a supply-chain security risk. Policy guardrails - How to ensure the agentic coder is compliant with the policies of the organization. Task-alignment - How to align the agentic coder on its tasks and goals. We introduce Agentic Process Evidence (APE), a signed, tamper-evident, machine-readable attestation of agentic processes, linking the sessions to their outcome (process-aware logging). APE enables Policy-as-Code control over the agentic processes, allowing for human in the loop only when it's needed. We support the in-toto style attestation framework, and the protocol is aligned with the relevant regulations

title: Dissipative controller as a hidden source of errors in quantum gates
abstract: Quantum systems are typically controlled by classical devices that necessarily dissipate energy to the surrounding environment. By the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, this implies noise in the control field produced. We investigate the relationship between the resulting errors and the entropy produced by the macroscopic controller, working in the context of a concrete minimal model. In the most experimentally relevant regime of fast control and high fidelity, we find a tradeoff between dissipation and control errors. These findings are exemplified by perturbative calculations of the gate fidelity for simple gate implementations and of the fidelity of state transfer via shortcuts to adiabaticity in the Landau-Zener model. Our results quantitatively demonstrate that suppressing errors in quantum control typically comes at the cost of macroscopic dissipation, which is needed to tame fluctuations in the classical controller.

title: Uncertainty-aware Coarse-to-Fine Main Pancreatic Duct Segmentation for Width Measurement in 3D MRCP
abstract: Assessment of the main pancreatic duct (MPD) from volumetric magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) scans is an essential task for ductal dilatation diagnosis and pancreatic cancer analysis. However, manual assessment is affected by reader variability in which automated analysis may assist. Nevertheless, fully automated and uncertainty-aware MPD analysis from volumetric MRCP remains underexplored area of research. In this study, we propose an automatic and uncertainty-aware deep learning-based pipeline for MPD segmentation and maximum-width analysis from MRCP scans. A coarse localisation model first identifies the ductal region-of-interest, followed by a fine model that segments the MPD within the region. The dataset consists of 256 MPD-segmented MRCP scans from 69 patients. A randomly selected holdout test subset of 14 patients with 55 MRCP volumes was used for evaluation. We employed a five-model cross-validation ensemble for improved performance and uncertainty estimation. The best MPD segmentation performance was 0.634 DSC, 0.744 precision, and 0.593 recall. The mean absolute error for maximum MPD width prediction was 0.355~mm and dilated MPD ($\geq 5$~mm) was detected with 75.0\% sensitivity and 74.4\% specificity. These novel results suggest that automated MPD segmentation can be used to aid MRCP-based duct measurements.

title: Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces
abstract: We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface. Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve. Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is constant in linear series on K3 surfaces.

title: Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles
abstract: Robot foundation models increasingly rely on flow-based action generation for general-purpose manipulation, yet the generated actions are not guaranteed to satisfy physical constraints such as joint limits and collision avoidance. This problem is especially challenging when the feasible set cannot be described analytically and is accessible only through black-box feasibility oracles. We study this practical oracle-only setting and propose an oracle-guided differentiable safeguard for safe flow-matching robot policies. The safeguard uses binary feasibility queries to correct unsafe updates in the forward pass, while extracting local boundary information to provide constraint-aware learning signals in the backward pass. Combined with discrete-time flow matching, the same safeguard is used during training and inference, enabling forward--backward aligned policy learning without explicit or differentiable constraint models. Experiments on obstacle-aware robotic manipulation demonstrate 100% constraint satisfaction while preserving task performance.

title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
abstract: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.

title: Disentangling Spin-induced Precession vs. Eccentricity in GW190521 and GW231123
abstract: We use the more than 2000 full numerical-relativity simulations included in the fifth release of the RIT binary-black-hole waveform catalog to perform Bayesian parameter estimation, via the rapid iterative fitting algorithm (RIFT), for the gravitational-wave events GW190521 and GW231123. We revisit GW190521, which has previously been identified as potentially possessing large eccentricity upon entering the detector band at $20~\mathrm{Hz}$, and confirm this finding: the highest likelihood is obtained from waveforms that are simultaneously eccentric and spin-precessing, yielding $e_{20} =0.207_{-0.147}^{+0.192}$ and $χ_{1,\perp}=0.717_{-0.406}^{+0.194}$. Applying the same simulation pool to GW231123, we likewise find a preference for spin precession where at 20 Hz $χ_{1,\perp}=0.678_{-0.462}^{+0.218}$, but in this case with negligible eccentricity at both $10~\mathrm{Hz}$ and $20~\mathrm{Hz}$, with $e_{10}=0.097_{-0.073}^{+0.124}$ and $e_{20}=0.056_{-0.045}^{+0.059}$. For comparison, both events are also analyzed using exclusively non-precessing (eccentric and quasi-circular) simulations, which yield lower likelihoods in each case. These results indicate that our approach is capable of discriminating between the effects of eccentricity and spin precession in current gravitational-wave signals. The singled out top peak likelihood NR simulations give estimates of the recoil velocities of the merged final holes of 3965km/s for GW190521, and of 2059km/s for GW231123.

title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids
abstract: Military installation energy readiness depends on having sufficient resources to sustain mission-critical loads throughout a prolonged utility outage. This paper develops a method to help operators manage energy resources during normal grid-connected operation while preserving islanded readiness. A robust viability kernel identifies combinations of battery energy, fuel, and load-shifting capability sufficient to sustain critical load under uncertain demand and photovoltaic generation. A probability bound translates stochastic generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count selected to meet a specified availability requirement at islanding. Case studies for a fourteen-day islanding requirement at 0.999 islanding-entry availability show that advance warning of an outage can be used to prepare resources to meet a higher readiness requirement before islanding begins. The case studies further demonstrate that economic-only operation and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy can fail to sustain critical load for the required duration, whereas enforcing the resource-dependent requirement preserves readiness at a modest increase in modeled grid-connected operating cost. These results demonstrate how active resource management can preserve long-duration energy readiness. The framework also helps commanders understand how readiness changes with operating conditions, even when the available resources remain the same.

title: The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
abstract: Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.

title: An HDG-type discretization of 1D embedded blood flow in complex networks with Riemann-coupled junctions
abstract: We present a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for one-dimensional blood flow in arterial networks with Windkessel boundary conditions. The scheme uses a Harten--Lax--van Leer (HLL) numerical flux and implicit time integration. After spatial discretization, the complete network---including cell states, hybrid traces, junction conditions, and dynamic $\mathrm{RCR}$ terminal pressures---is written as a residual index-one differential--algebraic equation (DAE) and integrated with variable-step, variable-order backward differentiation formulas. The implicit formulation removes the CFL stability restriction of explicit schemes and allows variable-order, variable-step solvers. The resulting single global residual and Jacobian for the network and its terminal dynamics also provide a natural interface for monolithic coupling with external nonlinear models. We establish local solvability and a semi-discrete energy balance, and show numerically optimal convergence rates for both solution variables in the $L^2$ norm and the broken $H^1$ seminorm. The solver is validated against established benchmarks, including an aortic bifurcation and a $37$-artery network, and is further applied to a cerebral arterial network. Mass conservation is observed in a synthetically generated anatomical liver network of $8\,\mathrm{k}$ vessels, and strong-scaling studies are performed on synthetic networks of $50\,\mathrm{k}$ and $100\,\mathrm{k}$ vessels.

title: The coupled spread of information and potential-driven motion in evacuating agent populations
abstract: Whether a population evacuates safely depends on two coupled processes: how a warning spreads through it, and how that information moves people. We model this coupling with an agent-based framework, in which each agent's information state--susceptible, exposed, informed or reverted--gates its motion. Only informed agents respond to a global background potential encoding hazards and safe zones, while all agents interact locally through a Lennard-Jones potential. The total potential experienced by an agent drives an Ito stochastic differential equation. Tests show that landscapes with potential minima leave far fewer agents never exposed than in a flat, uniform potential control landscape, as informed agents driven toward the minima sweep past susceptible neighbors. In our tests, conduit routes raise the fraction of agents in the safe-zone minima, but leave greater numbers of agents never exposed, when compared to an unguided evacuation. This is attributed to conduits shortening trips at the cost of informed agents having fewer encounters with susceptible neighbors who could receive their information. Independently, the effective information transmission rate estimated from these encounters falls roughly sixty-fold below its well-mixed value within the first time unit, because state transitions create spatial mechanisms of net transmission suppression that mean-field closure does not capture.

title: A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials
abstract: Let $π_n$ be a uniform parking function of size $n$. We determine the scale at which its first $k$ coordinates cease to be close in total variation to $k$ independent uniform variables on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The distance is comparable to $1\wedge \sqrt{k\log(k+1)/n}$, uniformly for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and tends to one above the scale $n/\log n$. At the critical scale $k\simλn/\log n$, it converges to $2Φ(\sqrt{λ/π})-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. A key ingredient is the Lorentzian property of the occupation generating polynomial of parking functions. Together with a strengthened Han inequality, this yields a relative entropy estimate for approximation by the product of the one-coordinate marginals.

title: Magnetotransport experiments on side-contacted topological insulator three-terminal Josephson junctions
abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions have recently attracted substantial attention. The ability to study Andreev bound states in a multi-phase parameter space opens up exciting avenues for generating topologically non-trivial phases in superconducting devices. A particularly interesting case is the trijunction based on a topological insulator (TI), which is predicted to host Majorana zero modes for suitable phase configurations (Fu and Kane, PRL 2008). Here we turn to the platform of the side-contacted TI trijunction and present experimental evidence for a multiterminal Josephson effect. We study the transport properties and find typical features of a two-dimensional critical current contour (CCC) as well as bias regimes in which only a single junction remains dissipationless. We pay particular attention to these features and study the effects of magnetic fields on single junctions within the trijunction, where, depending on the field direction, the supercurrents show Fraunhofer patterns, SQUID oscillations, or a monotonic decay. We find good agreement with semiclassical simulations for a single TI junction that take into account the top and bottom surface states. We observe pronounced non-convex shape deformations of the CCC under perpendicular magnetic fields that reflect the flux buildup in the loop formed by our trijunctions and provide a simple model sufficient to explain the observed effect. Our results provide the foundations for future studies of Majorana zero modes on this platform.

title: Multi-excited random walks on general trees
abstract: We study multi-excited random walks on infinite locally finite trees. The model is described by placing a stack of ``cookies'' at each vertex, with one cookie consumed on each successive visit. As long as cookies remain, the walk is in an excited regime and makes nearest-neighbour steps according to a prescribed sequence of biases. Once the stack is exhausted, the walk is in a non-excited regime and moves uniformly among the neighbouring vertices. The model is closely connected to foraging ecology, where repeated visits to a location can deplete local resources and thereby influence the attractiveness of that location for future visits. We prove that the process exhibits a sharp phase transition between recurrence and transience. The critical threshold is determined by the branching-ruin number of the tree, which is equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the tree's boundary under a suitable metric. Our result substantially extends Zerner's recurrence-transience criterion for multi-excited random walks on $\mathbb Z$ [Probab. Theory Related Fields 133 (2005)] to general trees.

title: Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Accurate multi-organ segmentation in computed tomography (CT) is essential for computer-aided diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. However, substantial variations in organ shape and size, together with low tissue contrast and ambiguous boundaries, complicate the modeling of heterogeneous anatomical structures. To address these challenges, we propose a Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network (MCDNet), which integrates adaptive local structural enhancement with channel-decoupled long-range modeling. Specifically, we introduce a Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled State-Space (MCSS) block that divides feature channels into separate processing groups, allowing differentiated structural representations to be learned within an efficient state-space framework. Within each group, a Morphology-Aware Enhancement Module (MAEM) combines deformable convolutions with channel attention to adapt local feature extraction to anatomical shape variations. Group-wise state-space modeling then captures long-range spatial dependencies, and channel gating adaptively integrates the resulting features. Experiments on the Synapse abdominal CT dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of MCDNet, achieving an average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 81.61% for multi-organ segmentation.

title: Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity
abstract: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic invariant measure is subsequently established by constructing a generalized coupling through a controlled auxiliary equation. Finally, the results are extended to other types of viscosities as well as to different stochastic hydrodynamical models.

title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
abstract: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.

title: Neural Blind Deconvolution for Image Scanning Microscopy
abstract: Image scanning microscopy (ISM) acquires one scanned image per detector element, which are then fused into a single image by multi-image deconvolution to obtain a super-resolved image. Its accuracy, however, depends on point spread function (PSF) models that sample- and system-induced aberrations often invalidate. Since differences between the scanned images encode aberration information, we propose a training-free blind Deep Image Prior (DIP) framework that jointly estimates the specimen and the detector-dependent PSFs. The PSFs are parametrised through the detector geometry and shared excitation and emission PSFs, reducing the unknowns while preserving the physical ISM model, and a Gaussian pre-initialisation stabilises the blind optimisation. On experimental tubulin data, blind DIP recovers finer filamentous structures than multi-image deconvolution and DIP with fixed theoretical PSFs, while adapting the PSFs to the measurements.

title: Rota universality of shifts on trees
abstract: We consider shift operators on infinite directed trees. We prove that under very mild assumptions on the structure of the tree, the resulting operator is universal (in the sense of Rota). We show connections between the spectrum of the operator and the frequency of branching in the tree.

title: Simulation of non-stationary anisotropic capillary wave turbulence within the framework of the kinetic equation
abstract: In the present work, numerical simulation of the evolution of capillary turbulence was performed on the basis of the wave kinetic equation taking into account energy dissipation at small scales. For an isotropic initial condition, the simulation results reproduce the Zakharov--Filonenko power-law turbulence spectrum for the wave action, \(n_k \sim k^{-17/4}\). The main result of the work is the calculation of the evolution for a substantially anisotropic initial condition. The numerical data indicate that, during the evolution of an anisotropic wave-action distribution, a factorized spectrum \(n(k,ϕ) \sim k^{-17/4}F(ϕ)\) is formed in polar coordinates \((k,ϕ)\), where \(F(ϕ)\) is a function of the angle in Fourier space. In the regime of a steady power-law distribution in \(k\), the calculated collision integral vanishes with high accuracy in the inertial interval of wavenumbers (the region of the power-law spectrum). Thus, the work provides evidence for the realization of a new strongly anisotropic turbulence spectrum, similar to Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectra.

title: Upcycling Language Models for Multiple Specialized Domains
abstract: Effective multi-domain adaptation of large language models requires prioritizing relevant domain knowledge while minimizing interference from irrelevant domains. Existing approaches commonly use Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to train a separate adapter for each domain and combine these adapters within one model. However, they either weight adapters equally regardless of the input domain or dynamically weight adapters while still activating all of them including irrelevant ones. Additionally, while efficient, their low-rank structure limits performance. In contrast, upcycling is a model expansion method that adds experts and a router to a dense Transformer layer offering larger capacity than LoRA approaches. In this paper, we propose Domain-Specialized Upcycling (DS-Upcycling) for multi-domain adaptation. We introduce a new domain-aware supervision that allows the router to effectively learn to distinguish domains by selecting the appropriate experts. During fine-tuning on each new domain, we update only the corresponding expert and router while freezing all other parameters. Experiments show that our method achieves the highest average performance across the adapted domains compared to baselines while retaining general performance. With just 256 examples per domain for router supervision, DS-Upcycling achieves 90-98% routing accuracy after adaptation compared with 43-70% for routers trained without our approach.

title: Evolutionary tracks and isochrones of the inverse Hall cascade
abstract: Decaying MHD turbulence can exhibit an inverse cascade, which means that the height of the spectrum of magnetic energy in the subinertial range increases with time. However, there is evidence for a resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed. It is unclear whether this is caused by reconnection, which is known to depend on resistivity. Here, we show that in the Hall cascade, where no momentum equation is solved, and the induction term is replaced by what corresponds to the negative Lorentz force in MHD, there is still a resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed, but no such dependence is found for an analogous numerical reconnection experiment. This suggests that the resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed is not necessarily related to reconnection.

title: Static Response of the Strongly Coupled Electron Gas from Diffusion Monte Carlo
abstract: The local field factor $G(q)$ of the HEG describes how exchange and correlation modify the response to a static perturbation, and enters dielectric screening, effective electron--electron interactions, and the xc kernel of TDDFT. Accurate zero-temperature data for $G(q)$, however, remain limited to metallic densities, $r_s\leq10$. In this work, we present diffusion Monte Carlo calculations of the static density response function $χ(q)$ and of $G(q)$ for $2\leq r_s\leq100$, and describe and discuss the methodological steps that enabled these calculations. We show how optimization of the perturbing potential in the trial wave function has an important effect, as a poor choice can reverse the sign of the response. A closed-form expression is provided for its optimal value, together with the density dependence of the linear-response window. We further show that backflow correlations leave $χ(q)$ unchanged and that $G(q)$ depends only weakly on system size even at very low density, so that Slater--Jastrow wave functions and modest system sizes suffice. Together, these results provide a practical guide for future QMC calculations of response properties of the electron gas and real materials. Our results agree with previous DMC data at metallic densities for $q>k_F$, and extend them below $k_F$. They also agree with diagrammatic QMC at $r_s=2$. At lower densities, our results show that $G(q)$ develops a nonmonotonic structure at intermediate-$q$, where the response approaches that of the noninteracting gas. Quantitative agreement is seen with finite-temperature path integral Monte Carlo, suggesting that the previously reported finite-temperature structure is inherited from the ground state. Using a parametrization of $G(q)$ that reproduces our data throughout the liquid phase, we relate this structure to short-range order in the pair correlation function and the static structure factor.

title: RepConTUR: A Report-Conditioned Volumetric Multimodal Model for Abdominal Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Tumor delineation is required for radiotherapy planning, yet automatic segmentation is limited by errors, predominantly false positives, that distort dose and increase editing time. The radiology report accompanies the scan and localizes disease at the suborgan level, but existing text-promptable models condition on short referring phrases, and most operate in 2D. We present RepConTUR, a single native-3D early-fusion multimodal model that conditions volumetric abdominal tumor segmentation on the narrative report. We extend AbdomenAtlas 3.0 to a suborgan-level promptable segmentation dataset and generate report-based VQA pairs, yielding four report-derived tasks on the same annotations: referring segmentation (RES), report-grounded segmentation (GSEG), report generation (RRG), and visual question answering (VQA). We train RepConTUR, comprising a 3D CT encoder, an early-fusion language model, and a native-3D segmentation module, jointly on the four tasks. Across liver, kidney and pancreas, RepConTUR attains the highest Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), instance-wise precision, and detection F1 among the text-promptable baselines, and adding the report raises mean precision while leaving recall comparable. Against two vision-only specialists, nnU-Net and the report-supervised R-Super, RepConTUR attains the highest value on every in-domain metric for liver and pancreas and the highest mean DSC, recall, precision, and detection F1 over the four out-of-distribution public cohorts. Ablations indicate that conditioning on the narrative report raises detection F1 from 0.499 to 0.528 within the same model, that joint GSEG training raises RES F1 from 0.450 to 0.482, and that the native-3D segmentation module raises GSEG F1 from 0.139 to 0.528 over its 2D counterpart. Code is available at https://github.com/Oncosoft-Research/RepConTUR.

title: On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv Problem for $\mathbb{Z}_n^r$
abstract: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem is a classical extremal problem in discrete geometry. We prove that, for all positive integers $n$ and $r$, every sequence of $4^r n$ lattice points in $\mathbb{Z}^r$ contains $n$ points whose centroid is again a lattice point.

title: Reward-Adaptive Co-Evolution of Policy and Rubric
abstract: Rubric-based rewards provide fine-grained, interpretable supervision for open-ended reinforcement learning, where holistic scalar rewards struggle to capture multidimensional response quality. Static rubrics can lose discriminative power as the policy distribution evolves, while existing policy--rubric co-evolution methods rely on globally prescribed update schedules that ignore heterogeneous reward informativeness. We introduce RACE, a Reward-Adaptive Co-Evolution framework. At the group level, per-rollout-group training-signal routing classifies groups as informative, diversity-collapsed, or rubric-failed, updating the policy only with informative groups while caching rubric failures. At the phase level, event-triggered phase switching enters rubric optimization upon persistent reward saturation and returns when rubric-reward improvement plateaus. Rubric phases train the generator on cached pairs using a frozen judge and a scale-normalized pairwise-margin reward. Across both levels, online threshold adaptation adjusts routing and switching thresholds through proportional control. Under a unified evaluation protocol, RACE achieves the highest average performance and outperforms the strongest fixed-alternation baseline on all eight tasks, while improving rubric discrimination.

title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on Kähler manifolds
abstract: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected Kähler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.

title: Single-atom billiards in an ultracold bath with energy-tunable collisions and threshold-sensitive detection
abstract: Transport processes at the microscopic scale can differ strongly from their macroscopic counterparts, particularly when the environment is not a well-defined surface but an unordered thermal medium. Ultracold quantum gases offer a high degree of controllability and directly observable dynamics, thereby providing a versatile platform to study such transport processes under precisely controllable conditions. Here, we realize an energy-tunable single-atom collider by transporting individual cesium atoms at controlled velocity through an ultracold rubidium bath. The constant lattice velocity sets the directed contribution to the collision-energy distribution, while the lattice depth provides a tunable energy threshold for collision-induced transport disruption. By independently varying these parameters together with bath density and temperature, we separate the number of collision events from their probability to disrupt transport. Across a regime with only a few expected collisions per passage, the inferred single-collision ejection probability rises from small values to near unity as the collision energy exceeds the lattice confinement scale. The experiment thus converts microscopic collisional energy transfer into a binary single-atom observable and provides a controlled link between individual scattering events and emergent dissipative transport.

title: Harmonic Analysis on $p$-adic Unipotent Groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $χ$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$. To the character $χ$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_χ=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $χ$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_χ$. We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition. As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.

title: Failure of the $H^1\times H^1\longrightarrow L^{1/2,\infty}$ estimate for the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal function and applications
abstract: In contrast to Christ's theorem that the lacunary spherical maximal operator is bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ ($d\geq2$), we show that the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal operator $$ \mathcal B_{\mathrm{lac}}(f,g)(x) =\sup_{\ell\in\mathbb Z} \Bigl|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-2^\ell y)\,g(x-2^\ell z)\,dσ(y,z)\Bigr| $$ is not bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)\times H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ for any $d\geq1$. In particular, it is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, we construct two finite linear combinations of smooth, compactly supported, mean-zero $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$-atoms for which the ratio of the weak $L^{1/2}$ quasinorm to the product of the two Hardy norms is at least $c_d\log(N+1)$. This lower bound holds already for the supremum over a suitable set of $N$ dyadic radii. For $d=1$ this answers the case $p=q=1$ of a question in Borges's survey. For every $k\ge3$ and $d\ge1$, a modification of the construction proves that the lacunary $k$-linear spherical maximal operator does not map $(H^1(\mathbb R^d))^k$ into $L^{1/k,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. We also indicate extensions to certain hypersurfaces and to horizontal spherical averages on the Heisenberg group.

title: The Effective Kerr-Compton Tree Amplitude from Black Hole Perturbation Theory
abstract: We develop a new method to construct the tree-level Compton amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a Kerr black hole in post-Minkowskian effective field theory. Building on previous computations that required physical consistency of the amplitude, the method uses wave scattering functions from black hole perturbation theory to uniquely determine additional contact terms. We illustrate the iterative procedure by deriving explicit expressions up to sixth order in spin, including previously unknown sectors at the fifth and sixth orders in spin. The amplitude features complex transcendental structures and a leading dissipative contact term at sixth order in spin. We verify our result against known results in the literature and reproduce the one-loop tail result from black hole perturbation theory.

title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
abstract: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.

title: Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation
abstract: With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.

title: Continuous tuning of quantum critical behavior in hybrid Josephson junction arrays
abstract: We report finite-temperature scaling of voltage-driven quantum phase transitions in hybrid Josephson junction arrays. A dual-gate geometry separately tunes interisland coupling and proximity-induced superconductivity, providing access to superconducting, insulating, and metallic transport regimes. The critical resistivity and scaling exponent evolve continuously with electrostatic tuning. Where the three regimes converge, the critical resistivity approaches $h/4e^2$, consistent with the self-dual limit, while the scaling exponent approaches the quantum-percolation estimate. Tuning toward stronger insulating behavior raises the critical resistivity and shifts the scaling exponent toward the classical-percolation value, while both parameters decrease toward the metallic regime. These results connect scaling regimes previously reported in different two-dimensional superconducting systems through continuous electrostatic control.

title: Diagonalization and Undecidability in Semi-Thue Systems
abstract: We revisit classical diagonalization argument in the setting of semi-Thue systems, viewing computation as nondeterministic rewriting rather than sequential machine execution. Semi-Thue systems naturally generate derivation trees, making existential acceptance, reachability, and infinite derivations fundamental computational notions. We formulate acceptance and decision directly in terms of derivation trees and study the associated assertion, word, and infiniteness problems. We prove that the complements of the assertion and word problems are not recursively enumerable by direct Post-style diagonal arguments. For the infiniteness problem, we give a constructive diagonalization based on a fixed universal semi-Thue system. Unlike the classical approach, the diagonal construction is carried out entirely within the rewriting formalism: the universal system remains an ordinary nondeterministic semi-Thue system while simulating encoded semi-Thue computations, including self-reference. These results show that undecidability in semi-Thue systems arises naturally from universality and self-reference in nondeterministic rewriting, rather than from machine states or control mechanisms. This perspective clarifies the relationship between rewriting systems, recursive enumerability, and classical diagonal arguments originating in the work of Post and Turing.

title: Seven Years of TESS Precovery Observations of the Dwarf-planet Candidate 2026 ED$_{138}$
abstract: The trans-Neptunian object 2026 ED$_{138}$ was announced in 2026 October as the first dwarf-planet candidate in our solar system discovered by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) observed it in five month-long sectors between 2019 and 2026, four of them before its discovery. We subtract every Gaia DR3 star from these crowded full-frame images with the TESS-Gaia Light Curve (TGLC) package, then remove static residuals with a running median. Stacking the images along its predicted path detects 2026 ED$_{138}$ in all five sectors at 5-21$σ$, and at 34$σ$ combined. The TESS positions alone confirm the JPL orbit, and its brightness is consistent with the 0.08 mag fading expected from its increasing distance and changing phase angle.

title: AFDM-ISAC Design Amalgamating FMCW Radar and Carrier Aggregation
abstract: Carrier-aggregation (CA)-assisted affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is conceived for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. A frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW)-inspired dechirping receiver is developed to exploit the inherent pulse-compression property of AFDM chirp subcarriers for accurate delay-Doppler estimation. To further enhance sensing performance, a pair of CA schemes is proposed. The Type-I CA scheme improves sensing accuracy by aggregating echo signals across multiple CA bands prior to radar processing, thereby reducing estimation error with low hardware overhead. The Type-II CA scheme enhances range resolution by effectively enlarging the sensing bandwidth, where chirps from different CA bands are designed to form a continuous set of chirp signals. Based on this principle, variable subcarrier sensing and asynchronous sensing schemes are developed. For the communication receiver, the generalized input-output relationship of AFDM is derived under both fractional delay and fractional Doppler (FDFD) channels. To address the challenge of FDFD estimation, a cross-domain sensing-assisted channel estimation (CDS-CE) scheme is proposed to facilitate time-domain delay-Doppler parameter estimation and affine-domain channel coefficient recovery. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significant improvements in sensing accuracy and resolution, as well as in channel estimation performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: Apple Vision Pro: The good, the bad, the ugly
abstract: Apple Vision Pro (AVP), the headset Apple introduced as its first ``spatial computer,'' built by a single, vertically integrated vendor, entered the market in February 2024 and has since accumulated a fast-growing body of primary research spanning surgery, education, accessibility, design, and human-computer interaction. In this paper, we adopt the tripartite structure of Leone's 1966 film to organize a systematic review of this literature: we cataloged the validated, working applications of AVP (the good), the persistent technical and ergonomic limitations of a still-early-generation headset (the bad), and the ethical concerns and structural harms that follow from deliberate design, marketing, and deployment choices (the ugly). The review is built from a Scopus export of 218 records mentioning AVP, which we narrowed to 104 papers (2024--2026) with a primary focus on AVP, using explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria that we report in full, alongside a PRISMA-informed flow diagram of the screening process. We find the corpus heavily skewed toward validating benefits (medicine and surgery, education, and software tooling account for over half of the included papers) and comparatively thin on documented risks or misuse, a pattern we treat as a finding in its own right rather than a limitation to be explained away. We further show that several recurring issues, namely price, simulated social presence, and the gaze-tracking privacy architecture, resist a clean separation into ``bad'' or ``ugly'' using the published evidence alone, since both readings remain compatible with the same data. We close by identifying where the evidence base most needs to grow: independent risk and ethics research, bystander- and equity-focused study designs, and disclosure that would let researchers distinguish an engineering backlog from a structural choice.

title: Coupled Guidance for Flow Matching
abstract: Guidance methods are essential tools for steering the generation process in diffusion models, improving the generalizability of stochastic robotic controllers and enabling high-quality controlled image synthesis. Despite strong parallels between flow-matching and diffusion, integrating guidance into flow-matching models remains quite challenging. Recent work has proposed general guidance frameworks for flow-matching, however, they are direct adaptations of diffusion guidance methods and can prove unstable. In this work, we conduct a theoretical analysis of guidance in flow-matching and show that a naive translation of diffusion-based guidance to flow-matching breaks the coupling distribution used during training, resulting in weaker control over sampling accuracy. Building on this insight, we propose Coupled Guidance, a flow-matching-specific guidance mechanism derived from a geometric perspective that leverages the coupling structure inherent to flow-matching training. To validate the effectiveness of our approach, we conduct extensive experimentation on a custom robotic collision avoidance task using ManiSkill3, four robotic dexterous manipulation tasks from the Adroit benchmark, and three image generation tasks, namely inpainting, super-resolution, and deblurring, using the ImageNet-128 and CelebA-HQ-256 datasets. Our findings show that our framework improves sample quality and guidance stability across all tasks, without imposing any additional overhead.

title: D-MOD: Diffusion mode estimation for accelerated MRI
abstract: Diffusion models are powerful priors for accelerated MRI reconstruction, but most current methods are posterior samplers, which return a random draw from the posterior. A reproducible and high-quality reconstruction often requires averaging many samples, resulting in a high computational cost. We introduce D-MOD, a fast algorithm that instead provides a posterior mode. It uses a minorize-maximize algorithm on a lower bound of the smoothed log-posterior, which provably increases the objective. Each iteration draws S noisy samples of the current estimate at the current noise level, denoises them with a pretrained diffusion model, and combines their average with the measured k-space through a conjugate-gradient (CG) solve. We anneal the noise levels, as the distance between the bound and its target decays quadratically with noise. On fastMRI brain (T1, T2, FLAIR), a single D-MOD reconstruction exceeds, in PSNR, the 10-sample finite-MMSE estimates of DPS, DAPS and SNORE-P and stays within 0.31 dB of the strongest baselines (DiffPIR, DDS). This approach thus provides a fast deterministic reconstruction algorithm (11-73 times faster than MMSE estimates), which is useful in a clinical setting.

title: Inverse Problem Approach for Non-Perturbative QCD: Applications
abstract: In arXiv:2211.13753 we proposed a novel theoretical approach for non-perturbative QCD, named the inverse problem approach. It extracts non-perturbative quantities by solving a dispersion integral equation as an inverse problem, using perturbative QCD and operator product expansion as inputs. In this work, we apply this approach to the pion and $a_1(1260)$ decay constants, as well as the continuum spectral function. The extracted $f_π= 130.8 \pm 8.1$ MeV agrees with the experimental value, and the reconstructed spectral function reproduces the ALEPH $τ$-decay data from threshold up to $s \simeq 3$ GeV$^2$. The advantages of this approach are as follows: (i) the whole non-perturbative range is solved simultaneously, yielding the ground state, excited states, and the continuum spectrum within a single framework; (ii) it is based on rigorous mathematics, with not only statistical but also systematic uncertainties well controlled and quantifiable; (iii) the regularized solutions exhibit convergence, allowing the precision to be systematically improved with better inputs; (iv) quark-hadron duality emerges naturally at high energy scales, avoiding the low-energy duality assumption and the Borel transformation, and eliminating their associated uncertainties. Finally, the successful physical application of the inverse problem approach demonstrates its broad applicability to non-perturbative quantities.

title: Beyond IPS: Reliable Counterfactual Evaluation in Multi-Stage Ad Systems without Logged Propensities
abstract: Offline evaluation of ad-ranking policies in multi-stage delivery systems is challenging because action propensities are often unavailable, limiting inverse propensity scoring (IPS). Reward-model-based estimators such as the Direct Method (DM) avoid propensities but can be biased when candidate policies induce impression distributions that differ from the logged data. We formalize DM-based counterfactual replay and propose mixture-weighted reward modeling, which reweights logged data toward a mixture of candidate-policy distributions using density ratios from a multiclass domain classifier. We bound each candidate's value-estimation error by overlap, cold-start, and replay terms, and derive an asymptotic rule that uses the cold-start mass to decide whether to trust offline selection or route candidates to online A/B testing. On an ads-delivery simulator and on production traffic from a large-scale CTR ranking system, the mixture-weighted reward model improves policy selection over its unweighted counterpart in both settings, with the largest gains at low overlap in simulation. Combined with a doubly robust correction, it attains the highest Top-1 accuracy in production and at low and medium overlap in simulation.

title: Non-Gaussian transport in tempered fractional Laplace motion
abstract: We study a minimal stochastic model for active transport featuring a non-Gaussian displacement probability density function and transient superdiffusion. Our approach is based on a combination of an exponential tempering in the parental fractional Brownian noise correlations, augmented by a gamma-distribution of the diffusivity across the ensemble. For the resulting tempered fractional Laplace motion we derive analytical expressions for the mean-squared displacement, the kurtosis, the non-Gaussianity parameter and the displacement probability density function. We also show via stochastic simulations that the model quantitatively reproduces the main experimental observations in a recent study of active cargo particle transport by a carpet of amoeba cells.

title: The dark surface of (163693) Atira and implications for inner-Earth asteroid origins
abstract: We compare the physical properties of inner-Earth asteroid (163693) Atira with the NEOMOD3 population model. Its radar-derived diameter of 4.9 km and absolute magnitude H$_V\simeq$16.4 imply a geometric albedo of p$_V\sim$0.02. Photometry with the Astrophysical Research Consortium 3.5-m telescope and ARCTIC yields g-r=0.49$\pm$0.03, r-i=0.20$\pm$0.02, i-z=0.02$\pm$0.03, a$^\ast$=$-0.05\pm0.03$, and a g-to-i spectral slope of 3.4$\pm$0.9$\%$/100 nm. The photometric reflectance favors a provisional X-type classification; combined with the low albedo, it supports a Tholen P-type interpretation. NEOMOD3 assigns an approximately 66$\%$ probability of delivery through inner Main Belt channels and 26$\%$ to central and outer Main Belt channels. Atira's NEOMOD3 albedo-category probabilities are $0.07\pm0.02$, $0.64\pm0.04$, and $0.29\pm0.04$ for p$_V<$0.1, 0.1$\leq$p$_V<$0.3, and p$_V\geq$0.3, respectively. Across 38 inner-Earth objects, including Atira and 'Ayló'chaxnim, inner Main Belt delivery generally dominates, and intermediate albedo is favored for 33 objects. Atira therefore represents an uncommon low-albedo outcome, compatible with delivery of dark material from the inner Main Belt or more distant primitive populations. Further characterization of inner-Earth asteroids will test whether current population models reproduce their compositional diversity.

title: SelfThinker: Self-Evolving Reasoning via Reliability-Verified Intrinsic Visual Thoughts
abstract: Unified multimodal models can both generate and understand images within a single set of weights, offering an opportunity to use image synthesis as training supervision for visual comprehension. However, existing visual chain-of-thought methods rely on human-annotated helper images during training and require slow image generation at test time. We present SelfThinker, the first self-evolving framework that turns a unified model's self-generated visual thoughts into stronger understanding without human image annotations. Given a visual problem, SelfThinker samples candidate helper images from its generation pathway and uses its frozen understanding pathway to score each candidate via conditional pointwise mutual information. High-utility visual thoughts then refine the generator via flow matching and serve as privileged teacher context for on-policy self-distillation. At inference, SelfThinker reasons directly from the original image in text without generating intermediate images. Although trained only on small synthetic visual-search and navigation datasets, SelfThinker transfers broadly to natural-image and spatial benchmarks, raising the seven-benchmark average of ThinkMorph-7B from 52.7 to 64.0 (+11.3 points). Controlled image-perturbation probes further show that SelfThinker surpasses ThinkMorph-7B by up to 40.4 points and its pretrained BAGEL-7B backbone by up to 23.2 points across fine-grained and spatial perception tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/zhangquanchen/SelfThinker.

title: Dual-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Vehicle Scheduling and Multi-Energy Dispatch in Electric-Hydrogen-Transport Systems
abstract: Electric-hydrogen-transport systems (EHTSs) require coordinated scheduling of electric and hydrogen vehicles together with multi-energy dispatch. These operations form a sequential decision process: upstream vehicle scheduling (VS) determines service allocation and order, thereby endogenously shaping the electricity and hydrogen demands faced by downstream energy dispatch (ED). This paper develops a dual-agent reinforcement learning framework tailored to the heterogeneous decision structures. The vehicle-scheduling agent combines proximal policy optimisation (PPO) with a Plackett-Luce policy to learn vehicle-priority permutations, which are then mapped to feasible charger and refueller assignments through a greedy allocation. The energy-dispatch agent employs twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) for continuous storage and energy-flow control. The directional coupling between the two decision layers is analysed, revealing that updates to the upstream scheduling policy can shift the demand distribution experienced by the downstream dispatcher. A three-stage training mechanism is therefore introduced, combining layer-wise pretraining with concurrent fine-tuning to mitigate the effects of scheduling-induced distribution shifts on downstream ED learning. Year-long case studies show that the proposed framework achieves the lowest vehicle-service delay and energy cost among the 11 evaluated methods, demonstrating effective coordination between vehicle scheduling and multi-energy dispatch.

title: Adiabatic Variational Principle: Born-Oppenheimer Theory for Emergent Electronic-Order Dynamics
abstract: Recent advances in microscopic many-body methods have enabled increasingly accurate descriptions of equilibrium quantum states, yet large-scale simulations of emergent-order dynamics typically rely on phenomenological equations with prescribed free-energy functionals. We introduce the Adiabatic Variational Principle (AVP), a framework for deriving order-parameter dynamics directly from an interacting many-body Hamiltonian. When microscopic relaxation is fast compared with order-parameter evolution, the many-body state follows the collective configuration adiabatically, in analogy with the Born--Oppenheimer separation of electronic and nuclear motion. This assumption makes explicit the adiabatic closure implicit in conventional phase-field descriptions. Each instantaneous order-parameter configuration then defines a constrained quasi-stationary many-body state, and the Lagrange multipliers enforcing these constraints directly provide the thermodynamic forces driving the collective evolution. Nonlinear Mori--Zwanzig projection theory further connects the reversible dynamics to the microscopic algebra of the collective variables and relates dissipation and fluctuations to the eliminated degrees of freedom. Applications to charge- and spin-density-wave dynamics recover Allen--Cahn domain growth, resolve evolving domain networks together with their microscopic electronic structure, and yield generalized Landau--Lifshitz dynamics for itinerant magnetism. The AVP thus provides a solver-independent microscopic foundation for phase-field-like simulations of the nonequilibrium dynamics of emergent electronic order.

title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators.

title: SynthFaces: Balanced Large Scale Human Dataset
abstract: The pursuit of fair and equitable AI in human-centric tasks is critically hindered by the inherent biases and privacy risks of real-world datasets, which offer imbalanced representations of identity and often contain sensitive personal information. Consequently, state-of-the-art generative models trained on this skewed data exhibit unfair performance, particularly in identity-preserving generation. In this work we propose a pipeline for controllable generation of dataset with diverse faces for generative models training and finetuning. We achieve this by expanding foundational Arc2Face diffusion model with a flow matching generative model in the manifold of identity embeddings. We demonstrate that such approach achieves both goals of generative fidelity and label diversity not present in real human-centric datasets. As a result we collect and further contextualize a highly balanced identity-centric dataset of humans named SynthFaces. By design, our released images and identities are synthetic, reducing direct reliance on real personal images; we empirically check identity separation with a nearest-neighbor non-leakage metric. We purpose it for training and tuning of fair models for various downstream tasks, and showcase its usability in finetuning an existing adapter-based method for personalized generation.

title: Asymptotically Compatible Variational Energy Dissipation Laws and Structure-Preserving Variable-Step Linear Relaxation Schemes for a Subdiffusive Tumor-Nutrient Model
abstract: In this work, we develop a mass-conservative subdiffusive tumor-nutrient model coupled through chemotaxis and memory-dependent reaction exchange, together with structure-preserving variable-step linear relaxation schemes. A weighted Riemann-Liouville identity is proved and used to construct a variational energy and the associated energy dissipation law for the proposed model. Both the model and the associated variational energy dissipation law are asymptotically compatible with their integer-order counterparts as the fractional order approaches one. For numerical approximation, we discretize the Riemann-Liouville fractional derivatives using the L1R formula on nonuniform time meshes and derive the associated discrete weighted inequality. We first construct a variable-step linear relaxation scheme for the subdiffusive model. Then, to mitigate alternating perturbations induced by the auxiliary-variable error and amplified by the L1R convolution at small fractional orders, we construct a temporally damped linear relaxation scheme. Since temporal damping leaves the auxiliary-variable recurrence unchanged, we further introduce an a posteriori relaxation correction to reduce alternating errors in the auxiliary variable. All three schemes preserve total mass, are proven to satisfy discrete variational energy dissipation laws using the discrete weighted inequality, and remain consistent with the integer-order limit. Several numerical examples are presented to validate the accuracy and stability of the proposed schemes.

title: Learning a Motion Manifold to Constrain Ambiguity in Unsupervised 4D Medical Image Interpolation
abstract: Unsupervised 4D medical image interpolation reconstructs intermediate anatomical states from temporally sparse observations without intermediate supervision. Distinct motion fields may attain comparable endpoint agreement while producing different intermediate anatomy, giving rise to motion ambiguity. This ambiguity is difficult to constrain when many independently adjustable motion variables must be estimated from the observed endpoints. We develop a framework that learns a motion manifold to restrict candidate motion fields while retaining sample-specific variation. Cross-Sample Spectral Basis Learning extracts recurring motion structure from endpoint-derived dense estimates and encodes it in a shared spectral basis. Sample-Conditioned Cayley Basis Reorientation uses predicted motion coordinates to rotate the effective motion directions for each endpoint pair without increasing the number of independent coordinates. Their composition defines a nonlinear family of complete velocity fields across endpoint pairs, accommodating anatomical and motion-state differences within a restricted representation. Integrating each predicted field supports bidirectional reconstruction at arbitrary intermediate times. Theoretical analysis establishes sufficient conditions under which endpoint observations distinguish nearby motions within the learned family. Experiments on ACDC and 4D-Lung demonstrate state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods trained without intermediate volumes and competitive results against methods using intermediate supervision.

title: xPRT: Cross-Passage Retrieval Pretraining
abstract: Dense retrievers are a foundational component underlying modern RAG and search systems. Training these models typically requires a curated collection of annotated query-document pairs, which are prohibitively expensive to obtain outside a handful of well-resourced domains. This has motivated a line of work that leverages large-scale unsupervised retrieval pretraining from unlabelled text alone. Most such methods learn by optimizing a language modelling or contrastive learning objective over short spans within a document. This raises the question: how can we extract richer learning signals from a single document for retrieval pretraining? To address it, we introduce xPRT (Cross-Passage Retrieval Pretraining), an unsupervised framework that learns from the key information distributed across an entire document and the connections between its parts. We evaluate xPRT against five state-of-the-art objectives on MTEB English v2, continuing pretraining from a public unsupervised checkpoint while holding the corpus, schedule, and training procedure fixed. Across diverse tasks spanning all task types, we observe that xPRT consistently outperforms the strongest baseline by 3.2% on an average. Notably, in this continual pretraining setting, many baseline methods incur substantial performance regressions, whereas our method delivers the largest complementary gains over the initial pretrained checkpoint. Controlled ablations confirm that xPRT's performance gains stem from its proposed cross-passage signals. xPRT demonstrates that a single unlabelled document is a much richer source of retrieval signal than prior work assumed and offers complementary gains to what current retrievers already capture.

title: Multistable nematic liquid crystal pores as reconfigurable optical vortex metasurfaces
